description: Add a count-agnostic real-file smoke test that runs parsePatternsBullets over the actual scripts/cam/patterns.md and cross-checks isResolved-selected bullets against an independent raw marker scan.

userStories.title: Add count-agnostic real-file smoke test for the patterns.md parser
userStories.description: As a maintainer of the patterns-archive tooling, I need one regression test that runs the real scripts/cam/patterns.md through parsePatternsBullets/isResolved and cross-checks the resolved-bullet segmentation against an independent raw marker scan, so that future format drift in the real file is caught mechanically instead of relying only on synthetic fixtures.
acceptanceCriteria: parsePatternsBullets and isResolved are exported from src/commands/patterns-archive.ts so the test can import them directly (a pure `export` addition, no behavioral change). [oracle: grep -Eq 'export function parsePatternsBullets|export .*parsePatternsBullets' src/commands/patterns-archive.ts]

A new test in test/commands/patterns-archive.test.ts loads the real scripts/cam/patterns.md from disk (not a synthetic fixture) and runs it through parsePatternsBullets. [oracle: grep -q 'patterns.md' test/commands/patterns-archive.test.ts]

The test asserts parsePatternsBullets returns a non-empty list of bullets for the real file (proving it parsed real content, not an empty read). [oracle: bun test test/commands/patterns-archive.test.ts]

The test asserts count-equivalence: the number of parsed bullets for which isResolved returns true equals the number of [resolved YYYY-MM] marker occurrences found by an independent raw-text regex scan over the whole file; the assertion holds for any count (0, 5, or 50) and is not coupled to current content. [oracle: bun test test/commands/patterns-archive.test.ts]
The test does NOT assert a hardcoded count of resolved bullets (no `toBe(5)`-style literal for the resolved count); it asserts the equivalence relation only. [oracle: reviewer-judgment]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Lint/static spine passes (bun run check:all). [oracle: bun run check:all]
userStories.notes: Files: test/commands/patterns-archive.test.ts (new test block), src/commands/patterns-archive.ts (add `export` to parsePatternsBullets @line 130 and isResolved @line 155; export the ParsedPatterns type if the test annotates it). TENSION: the issue's scope line says 'No src change / touch only the test file', but its own AC1/AC2 require calling parsePatternsBullets/isResolved directly and those are currently NOT exported (only RESOLVED_MARKER_RE, archivePatternsOnMain, and the interfaces are). The filer assumed they were already exported. Do NOT duplicate the parser into the test (that would test a copy, not the real parser) and do NOT satisfy AC2 via archivePatternsOnMain.archived (it only exposes the resolved count, never the total bullet count). The minimal correct fix is exporting the two pure helpers. GOTCHA (from issue): the SUGGESTION's original 'prove the 5 retrofitted bullets are selected' framing is STALE: those 5 bullets were archived to patterns.archive.md in commit 015dbc3e, so patterns.md currently has 0 real [resolved YYYY-MM] markers; never assert a fixed count. GOTCHA: `isResolved(block)` is literally `RESOLVED_MARKER_RE.test(block)`, so comparing isResolved to the same regex ON THE SAME BLOCK is tautological; the real value is comparing the parser's SEGMENTATION (blocks.filter(isResolved).length) to an INDEPENDENT raw scan (count of marker matches over the full file text via a fresh global regex, e.g. /\[resolved \d{4}-\d{2}\]/g). GOTCHA: only ~1 `[resolved ` substring exists in patterns.md and it is PROSE describing the marker format, not a real marker (the strict regex \[resolved \d{4}-\d{2}\] matches 0), so both sides of the equivalence are 0 today and stay green. Read the real file with Bun.file resolved relative to the repo root (bun test cwd is repo root); patterns.md is under scripts/cam/, NOT vendor/ or templates/, so no embed-vendor drift gate applies. Existing tests in this file already read fixture content via a fake SpawnFn; the new test reads the real file directly instead.
